newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel resumes East Jerusalem construction.
newsitem.headline: Israel resumes East Jerusalem construction.

text.p: Israeli bulldozers resumed work on Wednesday on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem that has plunged relations with the Palestinians into a crisis, witnesses said.
Israeli security forces remained on high alert to head off confrontations with the Palestinians over the construction. The first day of work on Tuesday passed without violence.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stood firm on his position Israel had the right to build on East Jerusalem land it captured in the 1967 Middle East war, despite Arab and international opposition.
In an interview with Israel Radio Netanyahu rejected U.S. State Department statements denying his assertion Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had sanctioned fresh guerrilla attacks.

"We have solid information from the Israeli intelligence," he said. "We see contacts of the PLO with Hamas and other organisations," he said, referring to the Islamic Resistance Movement that killed scores of Israelis in bombings a year ago.
"I want to say clearly. If there is terrorism we will see the Palestinian Authority as responsible," Netanyahu said.
